voice.name: Maya (workspace voice: West Yorkshire, warm, relaxed)

lines.text: An agent fixes a typo, then tries to force push to main. Guardrail stops it, and asks you first. You say no, and it tells you so.
Let's ship a feature with pi extensions.
lines.spoken: Let's ship a feature with pie extensions.

lines.text: You type five commands: plan, workflow, review, ship, and retro. And underneath every step, there are guards you never have to call.

Start with slash plan. The agent can read, but it can't edit. When a decision is really yours, it asks. Then it writes the plan, including how it'll be checked. And nothing changes until you approve it.
Slash until gives it a finish line. Here it says it's done, but the test still fails, so it's sent straight back. It only stops when the tests pass.
Now, a guard you never see. The agent says done, without checking. Done gate quietly reminds the model, so it runs the repo's own verify script before it claims anything.
Slash review looks for real defects, not style notes. It runs the command line, and catches a bug the unit test can't reach. Ask for the fix, and it proves it with the same command.
Slash ship checks again, commits only the files it should, and pushes once. Guardrail still asks, and this time, you say yes. And it's honest: passing locally isn't passing on CI.
Six guards run underneath it all: guardrail, done gate, diagnosis nudge, drift, deslop, and the router. You never call them. They're simply on, for every step.
lines.spoken: Six guards run underneath it all: guardrail, done gate, diagnosis nudge, drift, dee-slop, and the router. You never call them. They're simply on, for every step.

lines.text: pi extensions. Clone it, reload, and ship.
lines.spoken: Pie extensions. Clone it, reload, and ship.
